thesis: The Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF began trading on 2026-08-06 at $25.73 and drew $72M of first-day volume; five sessions later it sits within 0.3% of what the data feed reports as a 52-week high, which is simply the highest print in the fund's five-day life rather than a year's worth of range. There is no company-specific catalyst here to read: the move tracks sector sentiment around AI optical demand, and the fund's largest holdings (Lumentum ~15%, Coherent ~15%) are separately screened candidates in this same run, so a position would duplicate exposure the pipeline can take directly. This suggests the near-52-week-high trigger is an artifact of a five-day price history rather than evidence of anything.
invalidation: the fund accumulates enough trading history for a 52-week extreme to carry information, or it develops a return profile distinct from its two largest holdings
sources: SEC (Roundhill ETF Trust, Form CERT for LYTE): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001976517/000141783526000252/8A_Cert_LYTE.pdf

thesis: Corcept reported Q2 revenue of $256.1M, up 32% year over year, alongside full-year guidance of roughly $1.15B at the midpoint that came in about 15% above analyst estimates — a completed, company-disclosed result rather than an expectation. The strongest counter-case is the February 2026 Federal Circuit decision affirming that Teva's generic Korlym does not infringe two of Corcept's co-administration patents, which removes a barrier to generic competition in the base franchise; the 32% growth above was reported after that ruling, so the decision has not yet shown up in the revenue line, though it remains the main structural threat. Conviction is held at medium rather than high because a securities class action filed in February 2026 over statements about the relacorilant NDA is outstanding, and this run's research could not rule out a relacorilant regulatory milestone landing before the next review — either would be a binary that could reverse the read.
invalidation: generic Korlym competition begins showing up as sequential revenue erosion, or full-year guidance near $1.15B is walked back

thesis: Dell's Q1 FY2027 report disclosed record revenue of $43.8B with AI server revenue up 757% year over year to $16.1B, $24.4B of AI server orders booked, a record $51.3B AI backlog across more than 5,000 AI customers, and raised full-year guidance toward $167B including roughly $60B of AI server revenue. A separate confirmed catalyst followed in early August when AI cloud startup Volta named Dell as technology provider for a $10B, 133-megawatt AI factory in Norway. The stock trades within 1% of its 52-week high, so the obvious counter is that the AI server story is fully priced; the backlog figure is contracted work rather than pipeline, which argues the revenue is booked rather than hoped for. Conviction is capped at medium because Q2 FY2027 results are due 2026-08-27, an unresolved binary landing well before this position's next likely review.
invalidation: the AI backlog stops growing sequentially, or the 2026-08-27 report cuts the ~$60B AI server revenue target or the $167B full-year outlook

thesis: Rocket Lab's Q2 was operationally solid — record revenue, a narrowed loss, and backlog of $2.36B, up 137% year over year, supported by a $266M Air Force contract and a role in a $17B Space Force ceiling agreement. Against that, the 26% decline over the screened 60-day window is attributed largely to a sector-wide valuation pullback in space names, capital rotating toward the SpaceX listing, and the broader AI and chip selloff, rather than to company-specific deterioration. The company-specific negative that does exist is unresolved: CEO Peter Beck said Neutron will move to the launchpad in the fourth quarter, raising the possibility that the maiden flight slips into 2027, and shares came under pressure after earnings on precisely that uncertainty. A backlog-driven positive and an open-ended schedule risk offset each other with no scheduled event to settle them, so this run does not reach a clear net read.
invalidation: Neutron's first flight is firmly scheduled and confirmed for 2026, or conversely is formally pushed to 2027

thesis: In its first earnings report since the June Nasdaq listing, SpaceX disclosed Q2 revenue of $7.81B against roughly $6.93B expected, and the stock closed above its $135 IPO price on 2026-08-10 for the first time since 15 July after trading as low as $108.27 days earlier. The 24% decline across the screened 60-day window is therefore better explained as post-IPO price discovery — a newly floated share count finding its level, with a 2.09x volume spike consistent with that churn — than as a disclosed deterioration in the business. The June IPO is itself a completed equity issuance inside the last 90 days, which is flagged below.
invalidation: revenue growth decelerates in the next quarterly report, or the share price re-breaks and holds below the $135 IPO level

thesis: Microsoft's Q4 FY2026 report on 2026-07-29 was a completed, company-disclosed beat on both lines — adjusted EPS of $4.74 against $4.24 expected and revenue of $90.01B against $87.62B, an 18% year-over-year increase — with Azure revenue up 43% and Microsoft Cloud crossing $100B in annual revenue, followed by revenue guidance for the current quarter above consensus. Shares added roughly $450B in market value and are up about 25% over three sessions. The strongest counter-case is the AI-overspending worry that has been repricing the whole sector, and the fact that the stock had been down 19% year to date going into the print; that argument does not hold here because Microsoft raised revenue guidance while leaving calendar-2026 capital spending plans broadly unchanged, so the upgrade came from revenue rather than from spending more to buy it. No unresolved binary sits before the next quarterly report in late October.
invalidation: Azure growth decelerates materially from the 43% rate, or capital spending is raised sharply without a matching revenue guide

thesis: Cerebras reported Q2 2026 today, 2026-08-12: revenue of $209.9M against roughly $198.1M expected, a loss of $0.04 per share against $0.17 expected, full-year core revenue guidance raised to $880-890M from $855-865M, and core gross margin guided to expand to 38-40% on premium pricing for fast inference. That is a confirmed, company-disclosed result. The counter-case is immediate and unresolved: the stock fell about 14% in extended trading after the release, so the screened close of $262.06 predates a materially lower quote, and Phase B would be pricing an entry against a different tape than this signal was computed on. Because that reaction has not settled, the counter-case is named but not answered, which holds this at medium.
invalidation: the raised $880-890M full-year core revenue guide is trimmed, or core gross margin fails to reach the guided 38-40% band

thesis: AST SpaceMobile's Q2 on 2026-08-10 missed on both lines — revenue of $31.52M against $34.98M expected and a loss of $0.35 per share against $0.29 expected — while full-year guidance of $150-200M implies the great majority of the year's revenue must arrive in the back half. Operationally the buildout is real: BlueBirds 11, 12 and 13 reached orbit, the constellation stands at 13 spacecraft, production has advanced through satellite 42, and European integration testing has expanded across eight countries ahead of beta service. The company also completed a $1.15B convertible note offering in July 2026 at a $149.20 effective conversion price, with $96.9M spent on capped calls to limit dilution. A revenue miss against a guide that requires a steep second-half ramp, funded by fresh convertible issuance, is not a setup this run can read as net positive.
invalidation: beta service converts into revenue that puts the $150-200M full-year range within reach, or that range is formally cut

thesis: Lumentum's fiscal Q4, reported 2026-08-12, disclosed revenue of about $1.01B — up 109% year over year and 23% sequentially — with adjusted EPS of $3.23 against a $2.97 estimate, and guided the coming quarter to $1.225-1.275B of revenue and $4.05-4.35 of adjusted EPS. Shares rose about 14% on volume of roughly 8.3M against a 5.29M average, the 2.73x spike this screen caught. The strongest counter-case is that the stock has already run enormously off its 52-week low, so expectations should be extreme and a beat ought to be priced in; that does not settle the read here because the guidance itself implies another roughly 23% sequential revenue step and a further increase in EPS, so the disclosed trajectory is still accelerating rather than flattening, with an added regulatory tailwind from expected FCC limits on new Chinese optical transceivers steering hyperscaler orders toward Western suppliers. Results and guidance are both already disclosed, leaving no unresolved binary before the next quarterly report.
invalidation: the $1.225-1.275B revenue guide is missed or cut, or the AI optical order pace shows signs of a pause

thesis: Coherent's fiscal Q4 2026 release disclosed revenue of $2.05B, up 33.8% year over year, non-GAAP EPS of $1.74 against a $1.62 consensus, non-GAAP gross margin of 40.2%, and datacenter and communications revenue up 59% as AI datacenters shift from copper to optical interconnect. Guidance for fiscal Q1 2027 was set at $2.2-2.4B of revenue against roughly $2.13B consensus, with adjusted EPS of $1.85-2.05 against $1.77. The counter-case is that shares slipped about 4% in early extended trading despite the beat, after already climbing roughly 9% during the session on the read-through from Lumentum's report; that softness does not change the read because the guidance midpoint sits well above consensus on both revenue and EPS, so what the extended-hours move reflects is a stock that had run into its own print, not a downgrade to the disclosed trajectory. Results and guidance are both out, so no unresolved binary precedes the next review.
invalidation: the $2.2-2.4B fiscal Q1 revenue guide is missed or cut, or datacenter revenue growth decelerates sharply from 59%

thesis: Astera Labs reported record Q2 results on 2026-08-04 with revenue of $392.4M, up 104% year over year, and guided fiscal Q3 to $540-560M, roughly 40% sequential growth at the midpoint and above what analysts expected. Shares have nonetheless fallen about 12% since, which analysts attribute to the size of the rally that preceded the print rather than to the results themselves, alongside higher operating expenses tied to continued product roadmap investment. Read that way the 18% decline across the screened window is positioning unwinding rather than a disclosed fundamental deterioration, which is exactly the kind of explanation that discounts the move's significance in both directions and keeps conviction low.
invalidation: the $540-560M fiscal Q3 guide is missed, or operating expense growth continues to outpace revenue growth

thesis: Micron's disclosed fundamentals remain strong — record fiscal Q3 revenue of $41.5B at 84.6% gross margin, and 16 strategic agreements representing about $22B of customer commitments under take-or-pay structures — yet the stock has fallen from a $1,250-1,300 peak in June to the $900 area. The decline is described as sentiment snapping after a large AI run rather than an earnings problem, but it is not purely mechanical: Citi cut its target to $1,150 from $1,400 while projecting both DRAM and NAND prices decelerating sequentially over the next four quarters, and insider selling plus Chinese competition are cited alongside it. Contracted take-or-pay revenue on one side and a forecast pricing rollover on the other are genuinely offsetting, and this run cannot resolve which dominates.
invalidation: DRAM and NAND contract pricing turns down in reported results, or the take-or-pay agreements fail to hold revenue through a pricing decline

thesis: AMD's Q2 beat on both lines — revenue of $11.55B against $11.28B expected and EPS of $1.66 against $1.62 — but the stock fell anyway, and the reasons are company-specific rather than only atmospheric: the sales outlook missed the AI datacenter growth projections investors had built in, and shares sank further after a major customer said it would source AI chips from a rival. Those sit alongside a sector-wide derating in which the largest semiconductor names shed roughly $1 trillion in market value in a month, and a trailing P/E near 123 against a tech sector average closer to 35. A beat that is overwhelmed by a soft guide and a named customer loss does not give this run a clear net positive to act on.
invalidation: the next quarter's AI datacenter revenue guide reaccelerates, or the customer sourcing shift proves confined to a single product generation

thesis: Corning beat on both revenue and EPS in Q2 with optical communications up 32% on AI infrastructure demand and multiyear deals involving Amazon and Nvidia, but third-quarter guidance came in slightly below elevated consensus and the stock fell about 12% on 2026-07-28, leading a rout across optical names and posting its worst month in 24 years. A second, separate company-specific negative followed: reports that Apple scrapped a planned all-glass 20th-anniversary iPhone, which removes an expected demand source in display. Truist, UBS and Citi still rate the shares a Buy and read the selloff as an overreaction to tougher year-over-year comparisons. Two disclosed negatives against an intact optical growth story, with analysts and the tape pointing opposite ways, is an unresolved read rather than an entry.
invalidation: fourth-quarter guidance returns above consensus, or the lost Apple program proves material to display segment revenue

thesis: Nebius reported Q2 revenue up 454% year over year on demand for AI compute capacity, reaffirmed its full-year revenue outlook and raised power capacity targets, and separately disclosed a multi-year compute sale to Reflection AI worth more than $1B; shares rose roughly 28% on the session, the move behind this screen's 2.61x volume spike. Two things hold conviction down. The result was a GAAP loss, so the growth is not yet self-funding, and the company has been financing that growth with large convertible issuance — a private offering of convertible senior notes closed with aggregate gross proceeds of about $4.3B in 2031 and 2033 series, and current coverage frames fresh financing as an open question investors are actively weighing. This run could not establish the precise disclosure date of that raise relative to a 90-day window, so the dilution flag below is set on the conservative side rather than omitted.
invalidation: the reaffirmed full-year revenue outlook is cut, or further equity-linked issuance arrives before the current capacity buildout generates positive operating cash flow
